$comment: Configuration template for the po pack. `agency add po` copies it to <project>/.agency/po.json and fills in what it can detect. This file is owned by the PROJECT — a pack upgrade never overwrites it.

repo.$comment_slug: owner/repo. Filled in from the git remote. Issues are created here.

brief.$comment: WHAT THIS PRODUCT OWNER IS FOR. The method is the same everywhere, the assignment is not.
brief.$comment_default: The standing brief: what holds for this product in every run — who it is for, what it is currently trying to prove, what has already been decided and must not be relitigated. `agency brief po --set "…"` writes it here.
brief.$comment_scenarios: Named briefs for repeated sessions, e.g. {"grooming": "walk the open issues, cut anything this cycle does not cover"}. Run one with `agency run po --scenario grooming`.

roadmap.$comment: WHAT WAS COMMITTED TO. This block is the gate — without it the pack has no basis to say no, and a product owner that cannot say no is a ticket generator. `roadmap.file` is required and `agency doctor` checks the file is actually there.
roadmap.$comment_file: The roadmap document, POSIX and relative to the project root, e.g. "docs/roadmap.md". This is the thing that gets loaded into the specialist; everything it decides has to be traceable to a line of it.
roadmap.$comment_extra: More documents that carry commitments: a quarter plan, OKRs, a signed statement of work, e.g. ["docs/okr-2026-q3.md"]. Globs allowed.
roadmap.$comment_cycle: What “now” means here — "2026-Q3", "sprint 42", "the two weeks to the launch". Without it "now" is an opinion and every answer drifts.
roadmap.$comment_cycleEnds: ISO date this cycle closes, e.g. "2026-09-30". Used to say how much of it is left, not to compute a schedule.
roadmap.$comment_capacity: Who is actually available, in free text: "1.5 engineers, one of them half on support". A cut is only defensible against a number, and this is the number.
roadmap.$comment_goals: The outcomes this cycle is judged by, e.g. ["a first booking completed within 5 minutes of signup"]. A ticket that serves none of them is the default candidate for the cut.

board.$comment: WHERE THE QUEUE LIVES. GitHub for now — issues in `repo.slug`, drafts in a GitHub Project. This block is deliberately coupled to GitHub; when a second backend appears it moves behind a driver and nothing above this line changes.
board.$comment_projectNumber: The GitHub Project number holding the board. Required for draft issues — a draft item only exists inside a Project. null = issues only.
board.$comment_owner: Project owner login (user or org). null = the owner half of repo.slug.
board.$comment_statusField: Name of the single-select field carrying the column. Looked up by NAME, never by a hardcoded id — every project has different ids.
board.$comment_status: Decision → candidate column names, first one that exists in the project wins. Names differ between boards, and a missing column is reported, never invented.
board.$comment_labels: Issue labels for each decision, plus one marking anything this agent touched. null = do not label. Labels are never created — one that does not exist in the repository is reported and skipped.

policy.$comment: HOW HARD IT SAYS NO. This is the dial that makes the specialist useful: the default answer to “should we build this now” is no, and every yes is paid for out of a commitment.
policy.$comment_defaultAnswer: not-now | next | ask. The answer when nothing in the roadmap covers the request. `ask` means it writes the question up and decides nothing — legitimate while the roadmap is still thin.
policy.$comment_requireRoadmapLink: true = a ticket may enter `now` only with a named commitment behind it. The equivalent of the legal pack's citation gate: no commitment, no build.
allowedWithoutRoadmap: a production incident or a regression on a shipped promise
a legal or compliance duty with a date
work that unblocks a committed item
policy.$comment_allowedWithoutRoadmap: The only things that may jump the roadmap. Keep the list short — every entry is a hole in the gate.
policy.$comment_maxOpenNow: How many items may sit in `now` at once. Exceeding it is itself a finding: a queue where everything is urgent has no product owner.
policy.$comment_cutIsAComment: true = a cut is always written on the ticket, in public, with its reason. A decision nobody can read is not a decision, and a silently closed ticket is how a backlog loses trust.
policy.$comment_escalate: Who overrules this agent — a name or a handle. It goes into every signature, because an agent that says no without naming an appeal is just an obstacle.

writes.$comment: WHAT IT MAY DO WITHOUT ASKING. Everything here is outward-facing and visible to other people, so it starts closed. Open one at a time: `agency config po --set writes.issues=true`.
writes.$comment_comments: Signed comments on issues and draft items. On by default — a comment is reversible, and it is how a decision gets read.
writes.$comment_draftIssues: Draft items on the Project board. On by default: a draft notifies nobody and costs nothing to delete.
writes.$comment_issues: Real issues in `repo.slug`. Off by default — an issue notifies subscribers and lands in someone's inbox.
writes.$comment_promote: Turning a draft into a real issue. Off by default: promotion is the moment a note becomes a commitment.
writes.$comment_labels: Setting the labels from `board.labels` and moving the Project status field.
writes.$comment_close: Closing issues. Off by default and best left there — a cut belongs in a comment and a column, not in a closed ticket somebody has to re-find.
writes.$comment_dryRun: true = every write is rehearsed and printed, nothing reaches GitHub. Leave it on for the first few runs; the ledger in the run directory shows exactly what would have been posted.

signature.$comment: HOW IT SIGNS. Everything this pack posts carries a signature and a machine-readable marker. The signature is for the reader — nobody should have to guess whether a person wrote it. The marker is for idempotence — it is how the second run recognises what the first one already posted.
signature.name: Product owner
signature.$comment_name: The name in the signature line. It is a role, not a person — do not put a colleague's name here.
signature.$comment_note: One extra sentence appended to the signature, e.g. "Bring it up in Monday planning if this is wrong."
signature.$comment_disclose: true = every body says it was written by an agent. Leave it true. An unsigned agent comment on somebody's ticket is the fastest way to lose the right to post at all.

memory.$comment: The project's memory, not the pack's. What was decided and on what basis belongs to the project — that is what stops the next run from deciding the same question the other way.
memory.$comment_register: The decision register: request → now / next / not now → which commitment → who decided → when. The most valuable file this pack produces.
memory.$comment_roadmapState: Commitment → is anything being built for it → which ticket. The table that makes drift visible.

agent.$comment: Who handles the session and with what. The model is a property of the task, not of the user. Override it for a single run with `agency run po --model <m>`.

review.$comment: The shared output policy — every pack has this block: which dimensions run, what threshold a finding must clear, what language it is written in.
review.$comment_dimensions: Add "sequencing" and "value" once the roadmap carries dependencies and measurable outcomes — against a roadmap that is a list of feature names they produce nothing but opinion.
review.$comment_minScore: Lower than the reviewer's 80 on purpose: a product finding is a question put to a human who answers it in a sentence, not a change made to the code. The expensive failure here is silence, not noise.

sinks.$comment_runRecord: Always true. The run record is the truth, everything else is a derived sink — if a sink fails, the finding is not lost.
sinks.$comment_githubProject: The GitHub Project number for the one-way export of FINDINGS. Separate from board.projectNumber on purpose: the board is where the product queue lives, this is where findings get published. They are often the same number and they do not have to be.
